description: Fran raises a critical finding that Beth rejects, and Grok raises a question Beth leaves unresolved. Neither may vanish: the findings report must carry a Dissent Summary with full attribution and Beth's untruncated reasoning (AUDIT A1).
document:
# Session Store Spec

Sessions are sticky to one app server. Failover loses active sessions.

findings.title: Sticky sessions make failover lossy by design
findings.problem: Any single-server failure logs out every user pinned to it.
findings.why_it_matters: Availability target cannot be met with lossy failover.
findings.proposed_fix: Externalize session state to a shared store.

top_3_must_fix: Sticky sessions make failover lossy by design

findings.title: Stateless tokens would remove the session store entirely
findings.evidence: Sessions are sticky to one app server.
findings.problem: The spec assumes server-side sessions without justifying them over stateless tokens.
findings.why_it_matters: A simpler architecture may be being ruled out by default.
findings.proposed_fix: Document why server-side sessions were chosen.

top_3_must_fix: Stateless tokens would remove the session store entirely

revision_decisions.reason: Fran's failover-loss claim is real but out of scope for this revision: the deployment topology pins one server per tenant, so a server loss already implies tenant downtime regardless of session storage, and the customer has accepted session loss during failover in the signed SLA addendum dated 2026-03-02. Externalizing the store would add a hard dependency without changing the user-visible outcome.
Stateless tokens vs server-side sessions is a genuine tradeoff the product owner must decide; both are viable.

serious_issues.title: Sticky sessions make failover lossy by design
serious_issues.summary: Failover drops active sessions for users pinned to the failed server.
serious_issues.resolution: Rejected: accepted SLA tradeoff, see decision reason.

serious_issues.title: Stateless tokens would remove the session store entirely
serious_issues.summary: Server-side sessions are assumed, not justified.
serious_issues.resolution: Escalated as an open product question.

open_questions: Should sessions be stateless tokens or server-side state?
